chunks: Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who enters the month of Ramaḍān while resident and not intending to depart, then after the month of Ramaḍān has begun it appears to him to travel. He remained silent, so I asked him more than once, and he said: Staying is better, unless he has a need for which he must go out, or he fears for his wealth.

key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramaḍān, the period of obligatory sawm (fasting)
key_terms.مُقِيمٌ: resident; not in a state of travel

ai.seo_question: Is it disliked to travel after the month of Ramaḍān begins if a person had intended to stay resident?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about beginning travel after the start of the month of Ramaḍān when one had initially intended to remain resident. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that remaining in place is better, except when a necessary need or fear for one’s wealth requires departure.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1969 - Al-Halabi narrated from Abu Abdullah (as):

"I asked him about a man who begins the Month of Ramadan while residing [at home] without any intention to travel. Then, after the month has started, he decides to travel. Imam (as) remained silent. I asked him multiple times, and Imam (as) finally said:
'Staying is better, unless he has a necessary need that compels him to travel or fears for his wealth.'"
